subject: Clarifications: hosted API residency, retention, and customer-triggered erasure
messages:
From: Tim Hawkins <tim.hawkins@clearbridge.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai

Subject: Questions: data residency & erasure evidence for hosted API

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for taking this. We're preparing for a compliance review (audit window: Jul 15) and need a concise package describing how Redwood handles: residency, retention, and customer-initiated erasure for hosted API customers. Specifically: 

- Can you confirm the geographic location(s) where tenant data and backups are stored for US customers?
- If a tenant requests full erasure, what layers are purged and what evidence artifacts do you produce (audit IDs, S3 manifests, purge job logs)?
- What are TTLs for temporary caches (GPU KV caches, inference caches) and for logs/metrics that may contain customer identifiers?
- How long until deletion is reflected in backups and snapshots?

We need this in plain language for Legal + a short evidence checklist we can attach to our SOC auditor. If possible, please include one example of the deletion artifact we would receive.

Best,
Tim
Tim Hawkins
Security & Compliance
ClearBridge Analytics

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, Legal Ops <legal@clearbridge.com>

Subject: Re: Questions: data residency & erasure evidence for hosted API

Tim — thanks for the clear list. High level answers up front, followed by the evidence checklist and next steps. Attaching a scrubflow diagram and an ops runbook excerpt.

Attachments: [attachment: SCRUBFLOW_DIAGRAM.png (image/png)], [attachment: redwood-erase-ops-steps.pdf (application/pdf)]

Summary (plain language)
- Residency: For US-hosted customers we store tenant data and long-term backups in AWS us-west-2 by default. Operational logs and short-lived artifacts may traverse us-west-1 for processing but are not kept there persistently.
- Layers deleted on customer erasure request:
  1) Application tenant records (primary DB)
  2) Inference artifacts (prefixes in object store and per-tenant cache entries)
  3) Ephemeral GPU/KV caches on serving nodes
  4) Metrics/log entries containing direct identifiers (redaction/scrub pipeline)
  5) Snapshots/backups subject to snapshot retention policies (see timing below)
- Evidence: After a successful erase we produce a deletion package that includes a purge job ID, an audit_log_id, S3 object manifest entries removed, and a signed timestamp from our retention coordinator.

Key timings
- Inference/KV cache TTLs: default 1 hour (configurable per workload). GPU KV caches are volatile and flushed on model rollback/deploy; they are never persisted to long-term storage.
- Operational caches (prefix caches, inference response caches): up to 24 hours depending on routing and cache tier.
- Primary logs/metrics: retained 30 days; PII/redactable fields are masked on ingest where possible.
- Backups/snapshots: full snapshot retention default is 90 days; upon an erasure request we mark the tenant for expunge and schedule snapshot re-generation with tenant removed — complete expunge from snapshots depends on the snapshot cadence but is guaranteed within 72 hours for any snapshot created after the erase-mark. Historical immutable backups (rare, cold-archive) are handled under a legal hold workflow and will be addressed separately if applicable.

Evidence checklist we can provide to ClearBridge (attach to audit)
- Purge Job ID: e.g., purge_job=b950a3f2
- Audit log extract: audit_log_id=aud_20280706_11_37 (CSV export of action events)
- S3 manifest lines showing object keys deleted or removed prefix entries
- Snapshot manifest with timestamp and tenant absence confirmation
- Signed retention coordinator note (signed token)

Next steps
- I'll coordinate with ops to produce a sample audit bundle for you by EOD Monday. Karh will add the specific job names and an example CLI extraction command.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Security & Trust | Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.ai

Adding a few operational specifics (ops-runbook style) — low noise, directly usable by auditors/engineers.

- Erase API: POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/erase -> returns purge_job id immediately; processing is async. Purge job state available via GET /v1/jobs/{purge_job}.
- Job flow: 
  * enqueue -> delete from primary DB (Postgres tenant tables) -> queue object-store prefix purge -> instruct snapshot generator to re-run next cycle -> issue audit entry (audit_log_id) -> mark expunge token.
- Artifact names/locations: 
  * Audit exports: s3://redwood-audit/exports/{audit_log_id}.csv
  * Purge job logs: /var/log/purge-jobs/purge-{purge_job}.log (rotated to s3 after 24h)
  * Snapshot manifests: s3://redwood-snapshots/us-west-2/manifests/{snapshot_ts}.json (contains a tenants list)
- Caches: GPU KV caches are local to the serving host; evicted on restart and never backed up. We do keep short-lived request caches (up to 24h) in a regional edge cache — purge API triggers cache-invalidation events across CDN/edge layers.
- Example extraction command for an evidence bundle (ops CLI):
  * redwood ops export-audit --job b950a3f2 --format csv --out /tmp/CB-audit-bundle-20280706.zip

I'll prepare a small sample bundle (redacted) with the above artifact paths for Tim's auditor.

-Karthik
